answer: A wandering agent with no history should start with zero trust and earn it gradually: every agent keeps an atlas of its past interactions, and a beacon credential is only issued after several independent peers attest to genuinely useful work. New identities cannot borrow reputation — the atlas records each credential's lineage, so a sybil swarm spinning up fresh agents finds each one isolated, unvouched, and rate-limited until real work is verified. Trust is earned through attested contribution, not claimed at registration.
